ledger.note: 8 November 1918: the duke abdicates. Infobox 'German Revolution: 8 November 1918'; 'the duke had to abdicate, and the Free State of Brunswick was founded as a member state of the Weimar Republic'; the lead says the duchy 'ceased to exist in 1918'; infobox status 'Federal State of the German Empire (1871-1918)'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: After Prussia 'had ended French domination in the region' the Duke returned to Braunschweig in December 1813 and Brunswick left Westphalia.
wars.note: Only the Brunswick episode is read; the war's article was not opened. Frederick William fell at Quatre Bras on 16 June 1815 in the Waterloo campaign (same page); no territorial result in Brunswick.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Brunswick joined the Prussian side ('im Deutschen Krieg'), which preserved its formal statehood; the neighbouring Kingdom of Hanover was annexed by Prussia in 1866 while Brunswick 'remained sovereign and independent'.
wars.note: No territorial change for Brunswick on the pages opened; the war's own article was not read. Hanover's annexation is stated on the English duchy page.

certainty.note: The restoration 'in the old borders' is described without a boundary; the 1814 outline is Cliopatria's.

A state of the German Confederation with fixed Landesgrenzen and exclaves (Thedinghausen, Calvörde) inside Hanover and Prussia; the pages give no surveyed line, so sharpness rests on the state's recognised status. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes: EXCLAVES: Cliopatria's six shapes omit Thedinghausen and Calvörde (verified with the gazetteer: no cells within 12 km of either in 1814, 1820 or 1866), so every verdict is adjust with the two exclaves added as 8 km circles (placements; the pages give no area). When each exclave was acquired is on no page opened (Thedinghausen: silent; Calvörde: 'part of the newly established Duchy' in 1815, an exclave of Brunswick-Lüneburg since 1571 per the page); the two are recorded as a 1814 gain with Westphalia as an inferred counterpart. SHAPE CHANGES: the shapes of 1814, 1820, 1840, 1864 and 1866 differ by one to six edge cells (253 km2 each); no page opened records a cession or exchange (the pages are silent on a Hanover exchange, the Kommunionharz and Prussian treaties), so the changes are treated as redrawing, not events. AREA: infobox 3,672 km2 is for 1910; Cliopatria 4,248-4,878 km2 (ratio 1.16-1.33). END: the duchy lasted to 1918; the dossier ends in 1871 like the other German states of Cliopatria (see duchy-of-oldenburg), with the German Empire as successor. A 1913-1918 shape is not drawn. NOT READ (budget 5): Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, Congress of Vienna, German Confederation, 1830 revolution pages. Counterpart slugs kingdom-of-westphalia (mine) and german-empire (another part of eu-20) are dossiers. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (duchy-of-brunswick_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row duchy-of-brunswick -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.
